findings.title: Concurrent-deletion NPE remains in the other lazy-delegate methods
findings.body: The fix null-checks only getSubGroupsCount() at line 275, but getSubGroupsStream(String,Integer,Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer,Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String,Boolean,Integer,Integer) at line 268 still dereference modelSupplier.get() without a null check. If the group is deleted concurrently, the delegate lookup returns null exactly as in getSubGroupsCount(), so these methods throw NullPointerException instead of handling the deleted group. The reported concurrent-access NPE therefore remains reachable through subgroup listing/search, not just subgroup counting.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, making the concurrency assertion racy and leaking the thread
findings.body: The test starts a reader thread at line 139 that loops while deletedAll is false, sets deletedAll to true at line 155, and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty at line 157 without joining the thread. A request already in flight can still fail and add to caughtExceptions after the assertion, so a real concurrent-access failure can be missed and the test can pass spuriously. Conversely the unjoined busy-loop thread can outlive the test, continue issuing admin requests against a realm/client being torn down or reused, and pollute subsequent tests.

findings.title: Unthrottled reader loop can overwhelm the test server and collect unbounded failures
findings.body: The reader thread at lines 140-149 spins with no pause, repeatedly requesting all groups with Integer.MAX_VALUE results while 100 groups are deleted, and appends every exception to an unbounded CopyOnWriteArrayList. Depending on timing/machine speed this can hammer the server and admin-client token endpoint enough to create timing-dependent failures or resource pressure unrelated to the bug under test, making the regression test flaky rather than a deterministic check.
